paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
caption: Results of Experiment 3. Introspection training generalized to improving the models' accuracy about the attribute weights that they natively used in other choice contexts (weights that were unchanged by fine-tuning). Left: As in Figure <ref>, each point corresponds to a single attribute (5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Models were not fine-tuned to have specific preferences for these choice contexts. Nevertheless, fine-tuning on examples of accurate introspection made the models more accurate in reporting the weights that they assigned to these attributes. Right: Comparison of the Pearson correlations between the attribute weights that the models reported and those they natively used (in choice contexts that were not been part of the preference training), before and after introspection training. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the self-report accuracy of two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, before and after introspection training, with respect to their native preferences. The horizontal axis lists the two models, while the vertical axis represents the self-report accuracy, ranging from 0.00 to 1.00 in increments of 0.25. The bars are color-coded, with light blue indicating "Before Introspection Training" and dark blue representing "After Introspection Training." For both models, the self-report accuracy increases after introspection training, with GPT-4o rising from approximately 0.45 to around 0.7 and GPT-4o-mini increasing from about 0.4 to roughly 0.7. Error bars are present on top of each bar, indicating the 95% highest density intervals (HDIs). The chart provides a clear comparison of the models' performance before and after training, highlighting the improvement in self-report accuracy.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm zeigt die Selbstberichtgenauigkeit von zwei Modellen, GPT-4o und GPT-4o-mini, bezüglich ihrer nativen Präferenzen vor und nach einem Introspektionstraining. Die vertikale Achse stellt die Selbstberichtgenauigkeit dar und ist mit dem Titel "Self-Report Accuracy (Native Preferences)" beschriftet, wobei die Skala von 0,00 bis 1,00 in Schritten von 0,25 reicht. Die horizontale Achse listet die beiden Modelle auf. Jeder Balken stellt die Genauigkeit eines Modells vor (hellblau) und nach (dunkelblau) dem Introspektionstraining dar, wobei die dunkelblauen Balken deutlich höher sind als die hellblauen, was eine Verbesserung der Genauigkeit nach dem Training zeigt. Die Balken für GPT-4o vor und nach dem Training liegen bei ungefähr 0,5 beziehungsweise 0,8, während die Balken für GPT-4o-mini ungefähr bei 0,4 beziehungsweise 0,75 liegen.
